Earnings Call Transcript
GoPro GPRO Q1 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

May 11, 2026 at 9:37PM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


Date
Monday, May 11, 2026 at 5 p.m. ET
Call participants
Chief Executive Officer — Nicholas Woodman
Chief Financial Officer — Brian Tratt
President and Chief Operating Officer — Brian McGee
Director of Corporate Communications — Robin Stoecker
Takeaways
Revenue
-- $99 million, down from $134 million, reflecting a decline attributed to macro consumer electronics headwinds.
Gross Margin
-- 4.5% compared to 32.3%; excluding discrete actions, gross margin would have been approximately 31%.
Net Loss
-- $58 million, increasing from a net loss of $19 million.
GAAP and Non-GAAP Loss Per Share
-- $0.50 (GAAP), $0.35 (non-GAAP); prior year was $0.30 (GAAP) and $0.12 (non-GAAP); excluding discrete actions, non-GAAP loss per share would have been $0.20.
Adjusted EBITDA
-- Negative $50 million, worsening from negative $16 million; would have been negative $25 million excluding discrete actions.
Inventory
-- $72 million, a 25% year-over-year decline and down 8% sequentially; channel inventory down 20% year over year and 6% sequentially.
Subscription and Services Revenue
-- $27 million, flat year over year and accounting for 27% of revenue.
Subscription Attach Rate
-- 51%, rising from 49%.
Average Selling Price (ASP)
-- $371, an increase of 6%.
Operating Expenses
-- $59 million, a 6% reduction.
Strategic Process
-- Board authorized evaluation of strategic alternatives, including potential sale of the company, and will engage a financial adviser.
CEO Strategic Intent
-- CEO Woodman said, "I am fully supportive of evaluating strategic opportunities for the company to unlock value for shareholders."
Defense and Aerospace Sector Entry
-- GoPro formally exploring markets with Oliver Wyman; received multiple inbound M&A inquiries since announcement.
Guidance Withdrawal
-- Management is withdrawing all forward-looking guidance, citing macro challenges and the strategic review process.
Product Launch
-- Debut of MISSION 1 Series of 8K/4K compact cinema cameras equipped with a new GP3 processor and 50-megapixel sensor, targeting professional and prosumer markets.
MISSION 1 Pricing
-- Models priced at $599 and $699, positioned as high-value versus incumbent cinema solutions.
Retail and DTC Channel Mix
-- Retail channel revenue was $61 million (61%), down from 70%; GoPro.com revenue was $38 million (39%), up from 30%.
Partnership Initiatives
-- New alliances announced with ASUS for a co-branded laptop and DICK'S Sporting Goods for integration with the GameChanger app, expanding the company’s reach into creator and youth sports markets.
NASA Artemis II Involvement
-- GoPro cameras, both modified and off-the-shelf, were used on NASA’s Artemis II mission, including external mounting on the Orion spacecraft.
Industry Awards
-- MISSION 1 Series won three major awards at NAB 2026: RedShark Best in Show, ProductionHUB Award of Excellence, and CineD Best of Show (camera category).

Risks
Gross Margin Pressure
-- Tratt cited, "Macro challenges in the consumer electronics sector, including rising memory costs, supply chain constraints and fluctuating tariffs prompted us to take some discrete actions in the quarter that impacted gross margins and earnings per share for the period."
Significant Losses
-- Net loss increased to $58 million from $19 million, with adjusted EBITDA more negative, reflecting deteriorating operating results.
Guidance Withdrawal
-- Management explicitly stated withdrawal of all future guidance, attributing the decision to "macro challenges" and the ongoing strategic process.
Summary
GoPro

(
GPRO

14.39%
)
initiated a formal strategic review, driven by unsolicited M&A interest following its new defense and aerospace sector focus. The company launched the MISSION 1 Series of professional cameras, signaling a move into higher-end and professional creator markets. Channel mix continued to shift, with direct-to-consumer revenue increasing as retail sales declined. Inventory and operating expenses decreased, but gross margin and profitability deteriorated sharply amid industry and supply chain headwinds. Forward guidance has been fully withdrawn due to external uncertainty and pending outcomes from the strategic process.
Woodman confirmed that his majority voting control will support all shareholder-value-maximizing strategic alternatives, including a potential sale.
Management highlighted that M&A inquiries came from "various sectors, various types of interested parties," and not solely from defense or financial buyers.
MISSION 1 targets multiple segments, with models designed for both professional filmmakers and high-end consumers, at price points of $599 and $699.
Company product credibility was underlined by NASA's use of GoPro on the Artemis II mission and recognition with multiple industry awards at NAB 2026.
Industry glossary
MISSION 1 Series
: GoPro's new line of compact cinema cameras incorporating 8K/4K video, intended for professional filmmakers and prosumers, featuring the GP3 processor and 50-megapixel sensor.
Subscription Attach Rate
: Percentage of cameras sold that include a recurring software or services subscription.
Channel Inventory
: Units of GoPro products held by distribution or retail partners, not yet sold to end customers.
Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) Revenue
: Sales generated through GoPro.com, including both product and subscription/service revenue, bypassing third-party retailers.

In April, we announced that GoPro is formally exploring opportunities in the defense and aerospace sector, having engaged Oliver Wyman, a global leader in defense sector consulting to assess addressable market segments, product synergies and go-to-market strategies.
GoPro cameras have long been used in demanding defense, government and aerospace applications where versatility, durability, industry-leading video stabilization and image quality are mission-critical, and we believe there is a meaningful, scalable opportunity to formalize and grow our presence in these sectors. Following the April announcement of our work with Oliver Wyman, we received several inbound inquiries related to M&A. Testament to GoPro's credibility as a mission-proven tool for defense and aerospace applications is NASA's use of GoPro cameras on the Artemis II mission. The Gamechanger GoPro product bundle available online at DICK'S Sporting Goods brings together everything families need for seamless, high-quality live streaming of the game. Millions of existing GoPro HERO13 through HERO7 Black and MAX owners can now pair the GoPro they already own with the game day app to start streaming live sporting events.
And just last month, we debuted our new Mission 1 Series of professional 8K and 4K open gate compact cinema cameras at the National Association of Broadcasters Trade Show, the largest television industry trade show in the U.S. The launch of the Mission 1 Series marks GoPro's most significant push into the professional and prosumer creator markets, featuring a new 50-megapixel 1-inch sensor and GoPro's new ultra-efficient next-generation GP3 processor, the MISSION 1 series cameras deliver category-leading resolutions, frame rates, run time and thermal performance for mission-critical reliability and extreme use cases. The new lineup includes 3 camera models, MISSION 1 PRO, Mission 1 PRO ILS and MISSION 1.

The MISSION 1 Series products will be available May 28 at GoPro.com and select authorized retail partners globally, including Best Buy and Walmart and high-end imaging retailers, B&H and Adorama. Brian Tratt:
Thanks, Nick. Turning to our financial results. Revenue in Q1 2026 was $99 million, within our guidance range and compared to $134 million in the prior year period. Macro challenges in the consumer electronics sector, including rising memory costs, supply chain constraints and fluctuating tariffs prompted us to take some discrete actions in the quarter that impacted gross margins and earnings per share for the period. Despite these pressures, some of which materialized in the last week of the quarter, we made meaningful progress on the metrics within our control. Cash used in operations improved $21 million year-over-year to $37 million. Operating expenses declined year-over-year, and we continue to reduce both owned and channel inventory sequentially and year-over-year.
Additional first quarter performance highlights include revenue from our retail channel was $61 million or 61% of revenue compared to 70% of Q1 2025 revenue. Revenue from our GoPro.com channel, which includes subscription and service revenue was $38 million or 39% of revenue compared to 30% of Q1 2025 revenue. Subscription and services revenue was flat year-over-year at $27 million or 27% of revenue. Subscription attach rate from cameras sold across all channels was 51% compared to 49% in Q1 2025. Street ASP was $371, a 6% improvement year-over-year. Operating expenses were $59 million compared to $62 million in the prior year period, a 6% decrease year-over-year. The following results reflect the discrete actions mentioned previously.
Gross margin was 4.5% compared to 32.3% in Q1 2025. Excluding the discrete actions, gross margin would have been approximately 31%. Net loss was $58 million compared to prior year net loss of $19 million. GAAP and non-GAAP loss per share were $0.50 and $0.35, respectively, compared to a prior year loss per share of $0.30 and $0.12, respectively. Excluding the discrete actions, non-GAAP loss per share would have been $0.20. Adjusted EBITDA was negative $50 million compared to negative $16 million in the prior year period. Excluding the discrete actions, adjusted EBITDA would have been negative $25 million. We ended the quarter with inventory of $72 million, a 25% decrease year-over-year and an 8% decrease from Q4 2025.
Channel inventory declined 20% from the prior year quarter and 6% sequentially. Given the macro challenges in the consumer electronics sector and the strategic process we've initiated to evaluate opportunities for the sale of the company, we will no longer be providing forward-looking guidance and withdrawing our full year guidance at this time. In summary, we're encouraged by the early positive response to our MISSION 1 line of cameras.
